index.title: Trading tools
index.lead: Calculators and market views that do the arithmetic, so you can think about the decision.

needs.none: Works offline — no market data needed

common.enterValues: Fill in the fields to see a result.
common.noRates: No exchange rates are stored yet, so currency conversions are unavailable.
common.noRateForPair: No rate is stored for this currency pair.
common.comingWithData: This tool needs stored market data, which is not available on this site yet.
common.dataAsOf: Worked out from data up to {date}.

gainLoss.direction: Is this a gain or a loss?

result.breakeven: Gain needed to get back to even
result.breakevenNote: Measured against the smaller balance you are left with.

positionSize.riskHint: The share of the account you are willing to lose on this one trade.
positionSize.pipSize: One pip is {size} on this pair.

result.pipValue: Value of one pip per standard lot
result.needsRate: The position size needs an exchange rate for your account currency, and none is stored yet. The amount at risk above is still correct.

pipValue.priceHint: Leave empty to use the last stored price.
pipValue.pipSize: One pip is {size} on this pair.

pivot.manualOnly: No stored prices for this period — enter the figures yourself.
pivot.needsOhlc: Enter an open, high, low and close to see the levels.
pivot.tableHint: All five methods, side by side. They disagree on purpose.

marketHours.timelineNote: Session times follow daylight saving automatically. The market is shut from the New York close on Friday to the Sydney open on Sunday.

converter.rateTypeHint: Typical markups, not quotes, and not attributed to any named provider. They show the shape of the cost, which is usually larger than people expect.

result.midNote: The midpoint between what buyers offer and sellers ask. It is not a rate you can get.
result.markupNote: The mid-market rate, less a typical {percent}% markup.
result.costNote: At the mid-market rate you would have had {atMid} {to}.

correlation.caption: Correlation between pairs over the last {window}
correlation.empty: There is not enough stored price history yet to work out correlations. They appear once the platform has a few weeks of daily closes.
correlation.excluded: Not shown, for want of enough history: {symbols}.

method.statistic: Each cell is a correlation coefficient between −1 and +1. At +1 the two pairs moved in lockstep; at −1 exactly opposite; near 0 their moves were unrelated.
method.returns: We correlate daily returns, not prices. Two pairs both drifting upward look correlated at the price level even when their day-to-day moves have nothing to do with each other.
method.minimum: A cell with less history than the window shows a dash rather than a number. A coefficient worked out from a handful of days is not a small measurement, it is a wrong one.
method.cadence: The figures are updated once a day, from the last completed daily close. The page says when that was.
method.notAdvice: They describe a window that has already closed. They are not a forecast, and not a recommendation to trade one pair instead of another.

risk.reporting: {reported} of {total} markets in the basket reported.
risk.empty: None of the {total} markets in the basket has enough stored history yet, so there is no score to show. One appears once the platform has a few weeks of daily closes.
risk.historyNote: One point per day the score could be worked out.

method.score: A single score from 0 to 100. Above the upper threshold is risk-on, below the lower one is risk-off, and in between is neutral.
method.rank: Each market is scored by where its latest move sits within its own recent range — its percentile rank. A market that usually moves half a percent and has just moved two ranks near the top of its own history, whatever the absolute number.
method.direction: Markets that rise when risk is being taken on score as they rank. Markets that rise when risk is coming off have their rank flipped before it is counted. The weighted average of what is left is the score.
method.excluded: A market with too little history is left out and counted, never filled in with a zero. A zero would be a claim that the market was flat; leaving it out is the truth, which is that we do not know.
method.cadence: The score is worked out once a day, from the last completed daily close. The page says when that was.
method.notAdvice: It describes what has already happened. It is not a forecast, and it is not a recommendation to do anything.
